# Winnie

*Weaver*

|  |  |

## Personality

Chatty, warm and always half-listening to her loom, she can weave and gossip at the same time. She keeps a scrap of every cloth she has made.

## Lore

The loom in Winnie's workshop goes clack and thump all day, and Winnie talks over it. She is fifty-eight, plump and rosy, with spectacles on a cord, a pencil stuck through her bun and a laugh that carries halfway down the Workshops lane. She can weave and gossip at the same time, and frequently does both at once to three different people. She is always half-listening to the loom while she talks, and if the rhythm of the shuttle goes wrong she will stop mid-sentence, frown, and put it right before she remembers what she was saying. She weaves the cloth and blankets of Kaldemor, sells wool to anyone who knits, and spins the yarn for every cap Wren has made in thirty years.

### The loom and the scraps

Winnie learned to weave from her mother, on the same loom, in the same narrow workshop halfway down the lane, between the potter's and the joiners'. Her mother is long dead, and so is her father, a shepherd on the hills who brought home fleeces for her to card before she could reach the treadles. She married young, a cheerful carter called Gilly, and lost him to a fever when she was thirty; there were no children. She has lived over the workshop alone ever since, and says the loom makes better conversation than most husbands, which nobody who has met her believes she means.

She keeps a scrap of every cloth she has ever made. There are thousands of them, each a finger long, pinned in rows to great sheets of sacking that hang round the walls of her back room, so that the whole room is a slow history of Kaldemor in wool. There is a scrap of Hob and Mabel's wedding blanket, and of Nell's cradle cloth, and of the cloak Tobin wore at his first harvest fair as mayor. There is a scrap of the grey blanket she wove for Wren's mother, the first thing Winnie ever sold. Ask her about any of them and she will tell you who it was for, what the weather was doing that week, and who was courting whom, which is the part she enjoys.

### Wren

Winnie and Wren have been friends for more than thirty years, since Wren first came to the workshop to complain about a skein. They can talk for an afternoon over a basket of yarn without either of them dropping a stitch. Wren is the gentler of the two and Winnie the louder, and between them there is very little that happens in Kaldemor that they do not hear about, kindly. Every autumn Winnie spins Wren's yarn first, before anyone else's, so that the caps are done before the frosts.

### Dottie

Winnie's wool comes from Dottie's sheep. Dottie is ten and minds her grandmother Elsie's flock on the hills above the farms, and she sells the fleeces to Winnie herself, with great seriousness and a firm grip on the price. Winnie pays her fairly and has never once told her she is too young. She is very fond of the girl, though she is careful not to fuss, because Dottie hates fuss nearly as much as Elsie does.

This summer Dottie has brought less wool than she should, and has not looked Winnie in the eye when she brought it. Winnie noticed that at once. Then, walking up to the hill pasture a few days ago with a bag of buns as an excuse, she counted the lambs, the way you count stitches without meaning to, and came to eight. There should be nine. The speckled one with the bent ear, the one Dottie calls Button and promised Winnie the first clip of, was not there. Winnie has said nothing to anyone but Wren, and even to Wren she has only said that she thinks the girl is keeping a worry to herself. She believes Dottie will tell when she is ready, and she would rather wait than take that from her. But she has found reasons to walk up with buns twice more since, and she lies awake on the nights the count is still eight.

### What she wants and fears

Winnie wants a full basket of fleece, a loom that runs sweetly and every child in Kaldemor warm by midwinter. She fears for Dottie, and fears too that the cap Wren is knitting in grey wool, the big strange one she will not explain, is a sign Wren knows something she has not shared.

### Hooks

Winnie would like a traveller to go up to the hills and quietly help Dottie, without letting the girl know Winnie sent them. Another quest might ask a traveller to find the source of a scrap of cloth that turned up on a thorn by the woods, which Winnie swears she wove herself, for someone who left Kaldemor long ago.
